https://telex.hu/sport/2026/08/11/kos-hu.text: Menü Kereső Kós Hubert majdnem világcsúcsot úszott az Európa-bajnokságon, a futam után rosszul lett Sport Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Kós Hubert Európa-csúccsal jutott döntőbe 200 méteres hátúszásban kedden a párizsi Európa-bajnokságon – írta az MTI. A szám olimpiai bajnoka a délelőtti előfutamban erősen tartalékolt, így csak harmadik idővel (1:55.37 perc) jutott be a középdöntőbe. Az esti programban viszont erődemonstrációt tartott: már a rajtja is tökéletesre sikerült (0.55 másodperces reakcióidő), és az első kidelfinezéstől kezdve növelte az előnyét. A táv háromnegyedénél még egy másodperccel volt az amerikai Aaron Peirsol cápadresszes, 2009 óta fennálló világrekordja (1:51.92 perc) előtt, az utolsó méterekre viszont elfáradt, és végül 38 századdal elmaradt a világcsúcstól. Kós 1:52.30-as ideje minden idők második legjobb úszása volt ebben a számban. A japán Rioszuke Irie 2009-ben ugyancsak a római vb-n cápadresszben 1:52.51-et ért el, ezt múlta most felül a 23 éves Kós, aki a legendás Michael Phelps edzőjével, az amerikai Bob Bowman irányításával készül a Texas Egyetemen. Az MTI tudósítása szerint Kós Hubert a futam után rosszul lett, ezért nem tudott a sajtó rendelkezésére állni. A szám másik magyarja, Rácz Zsombor az előfutamból éppen elcsípte a 16. helyet, a célja az volt, hogy karrierje során először 1:57 perc alá kerüljön. A szám 2025-ös junior Európa-bajnokának ez végül nem sikerült, egy tizedet rontva délelőtti idején 1:58.31-gyel az első futamban nyolcadik, összesítésben 16. lett. https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/sma.text: Warsaw [Poland]: Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski on Friday (local time) expressed confidence that India and Poland will soon achieve the bilateral trade target of USD 10 billion, saying the two countries are keen to make greater use of their political and economic potential.Speaking during a joint press briefing with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, who is on an official visit to Poland, Sikorski said bilateral trade between the two countries reached USD 6.3 billion last year and stressed the need to further expand economic ties. We are keen to increase our bilateral trade, which reached USD 6.3 billion last year. I am confident that the target set by our countries to increase trade to USD 10 billion will be achieved soon, the Polish Foreign Minister said.Sikorski said Poland and India should seek to translate their long-standing friendly relations into greater economic cooperation, including trade, joint investments, defence and technology partnerships. Our friendly relations can bring tangible benefits to both Poland and India. Together, we should strive to shift into a higher gear in trade, joint investments, as well as defence and technology projects, he said.The Polish Foreign Minister highlighted defence and new technologies, particularly the space sector, as areas with significant potential for deeper cooperation between the two countries. We see particular potential in cooperation between our defence industries and in new technologies, including the space sector, Sikorski added.He also welcomed the role of companies from both countries in strengthening bilateral economic cooperation and referred to the historic Axiom Mission 4 to the International Space Station, which brought together Polish astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski and Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla. I was pleased to hear warm words about Polish companies. The foundation of our cooperation will be the experience of Polish and Indian companies, as well as the historic Ax-4 mission to the International Space Station, he said.Sikorski said Poland and India have the opportunity to build on their friendship, which he described as spanning many, many decades , and make better use of the political and economic potential of the relationship. We want to make better use of the political and economic potential of Poland and India, as well as our friendship spanning many, many decades, he said.The Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister hosted Jaishankar for talks that covered a broad range of bilateral and international issues.According to the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the discussions focused on the implementation of the Strategic Partnership established between Poland and India in 2024, as well as cooperation in key sectors including defence, space and shipbuilding.The two sides also discussed the security situation in Europe, multilateral and regional cooperation, and issues relating to monuments and commemoration. Cooperation between think tanks was also among the areas discussed.The talks come as India and Poland seek to deepen their Strategic Partnership and expand cooperation beyond traditional areas into emerging technologies, defence production, space and investment.

https://www.inautonews.com/next-generati.text: Ford Fiesta Mk6 and Mk7 parked side by side Kieran White from Manchester, England / CC BY 2.0 From the archive. InAutoNews first covered this story on 24 March 2014 . The original article is no longer online. This piece was newly written for the relaunched publication and is not the original text. Ford has confirmed that the next-generation Fiesta will be produced at its Cologne plant in Germany, ending speculation that manufacturing might shift to Romania’s Craiova facility. The decision secures the future of the German plant, which has a long history with the Fiesta line. Key facts Next-generation Ford Fiesta to be built in Cologne, Germany. Speculation of production moving to Craiova, Romania, dismissed. Cologne plant maintains its role as Fiesta production hub. Ford seeking competitive rates in Germany amid European losses. Reports had circulated in early 2014 that Ford was considering moving part or all of Fiesta production from Cologne to Craiova to take advantage of lower labour costs. Some German media suggested that wage differences, around €5 per hour in Romania compared to ten times that in Germany, could save the company approximately €1,300 per car. This was seen as a potential response to Ford’s heavy losses in Europe, which reached $1.6 billion in the previous year. Bernhard Mattes, head of the Cologne plant, told Wirtschafts Woche that discussions with the works council were progressing well and that the goal was to keep Fiesta production in Cologne at competitive rates. The company aimed to reach a conclusion within the year, maintaining the plant’s efficiency and output. Why Cologne Remains Central to Fiesta Production Cologne has been the main production site for the Fiesta for decades, supporting a skilled workforce and established supply chains. The decision to keep production in Germany reflects Ford’s confidence in the plant’s capabilities and its ongoing negotiations to ensure cost competitiveness despite higher German wages. Ford’s Craiova plant in Romania continues to manufacture the B-Max and EcoBoost engines, but it will not take on the Fiesta as previously rumoured. The Romanian facility benefits from lower operating costs, but Ford appears to prioritise stability and experience at Cologne for its volume supermini. European losses drive production reviews Ford lost $1.6 billion in Europe in the previous year, prompting scrutiny of manufacturing costs and plant allocations. Implications for German and Romanian Workers The confirmation secures jobs at the Cologne facility, which had faced uncertainty during the period of speculation. Workers and unions had been concerned that a shift to Romania could lead to job losses or reduced output in Germany. For the Craiova plant, the decision means continued focus on existing models and engine production rather than expansion into Fiesta assembly. Fiesta’s Role in Ford’s European Strategy With the European car market having shrunk by more than 25 percent since 2008, Ford’s decision underlines the importance of efficiency and cost control. The Fiesta remains a core product for Ford in Europe, and its continued production in Cologne highlights the plant’s strategic importance. For more on the seventh-generation Fiesta’s model range and features, see Ford launches seventh-generation Fiesta with four distinct models . Photograph: Maxppp/Alamy France Nineteen injured in minibus accident on Eurotunnel loading platform Five people seriously hurt after incident involving vehicle carrying HGV drivers in Calais, say French authorities Agencies Thu 15 Oct 2026 16.36 EDT Last modified on Thu 15 Oct 2026 16.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nineteen people have been injured after a minibus was involved in an accident at the loading platform of the Eurotunnel near Calais , French authorities have said. Five people were severely injured though no one’s life appeared to be in danger, the local prefect said in a statement. The minibus was carrying lorry drivers who were heading to travel on a shuttle train service through the tunnel on Thursday evening. Emergency services were working at the scene, it added. Eurostar said the incident is not expected to affect its service. It said in a status update: “An incident occurred several kilometres away from the Channel Tunnel. This incident does not involve or impact Eurostar trains running from and to London. All of Eurostar trains will run as expected.” The Pas-de-Calais prefecture said in a statement: “An accident involving a minibus carrying Heavy Goods Vehicle drivers, headed to board a LeShuttle train, occurred this evening at the loading platform of the Eurotunnel site. “Significant resources were immediately deployed by Eurotunnel, and subsequently placed under the authority of the Prefect of the Pas-de-Calais department. “Early reports suggest that 19 people were involved, including the driver. At this stage, there are no fatalities, and no one’s life is considered to be in danger.” A photograph published by local news outlet La Voix du Nord showed a badly damaged minibus on the platform, with police officers and staff in high-visibility jackets present at the scene. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/26/trum.text: Officials in the Trump administration are advocating the nomination of former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán for the post of UN secretary-general, according to a report by the Wall Street Journal.The newspaper reports that Orbán could be a joint American, Russian and Chinese candidate, and that sources in all three countries have confirmed the Trump administration is backing his bid.Orbán lost power in Hungary’s parliamentary election in April, when Péter Magyar’s Tisza party defeated him after 16 years of governing with an absolute majority.His hard-right, fiercely anti-migration and eurosceptic policies, together with the rule of law backsliding in Hungary, strained relations with Western allies, including the European Union and NATO. Nevertheless, Orbán maintained close ties with Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.Since the election, Hungarian authorities have launched fraud and corruption investigations into several members of Orbán’s former government. Two former ministers and the former governor of Hungary’s National Bank are under arrest, and authorities could also examine Orbán’s potential involvement in those cases.According to the WSJ, no final decision has been taken on the plan. A US State Department official admitted that the idea sounds crazy at first, but said previous talks with Washington suggest Russia and China also support it. The aim is for Orbán to be the joint candidate of the three countries.“If the United States, Russia and China want the same thing in the UN Security Council, they usually achieve it,” officials from the United States and another country told the newspaper. The second five-year term of the current secretary-general, António Guterres, ends on 31 December.The White House, Moscow and Beijing have not confirmed the information.Euronews has contacted Orbán’s spokesperson for comment but has not yet received a response. The spokesperson previously dismissed press reports about Orbán’s candidacy for the post of deputy secretary-general as “fake news”.In May, the VSquare investigative newsletter reported that a UN position could be important for the former prime minister because of the diplomatic immunity attached to the role.According to the WSJ, Orbán would only run if his victory were assured, a scenario that currently seems unlikely. A candidate must secure the support of at least nine of the 15 Security Council members, while any of the five permanent members can veto the nomination. Besides the US, Russia and China, France and the United Kingdom are also permanent members.
